correctness.rationale: Independence forces all positive labels into a single part. A zero or one inside that part has no positive neighbor because vertices in one part are pairwise nonadjacent, so every supported-part vertex must be labelled 2 or 3 and every other vertex is zero. Any outside zero sees the entire supporting part; for part size at least two every 2/3 assignment works, whereas on a singleton only label 3 works. Summing \((z^2+z^3)^{n_i}\) over supporting parts and removing the invalid singleton \(z^2\) terms gives the displayed enumerator, total count, and minimum-function counts. The package verifier exhausts all labels for every multipartite type through order nine and agrees exactly.

value.rationale: Although the complete weight distribution is a natural refinement of the minimum parameter, on a complete multipartite graph it follows immediately from two elementary observations: independent support lies in one part, and labels 0 or 1 cannot occur inside that part. The remaining polynomial is a binomial expansion with one singleton correction. Under the shared value bar, this is a routine definition-level specialization rather than a motivated structural gap requiring substantive mathematics.

final_claim: On a connected complete multipartite graph, every independent double Roman dominating function is supported on one whole part, labels that part only by 2 and 3, and is otherwise zero, with the singleton support requiring label 3; hence the all-function weight enumerator and minimum-function counts in RESULT.md follow.
limitations: The minimum parameter itself is already substantially constrained by published general inequalities.
The record's all-function enumerator appears novel in the checked literature, but the derivation is a routine definition chase on this graph class.
